name: 01 · C# from your first line
description: Understand types, null, decisions, and methods by reading small C# programs one line at a time.

name: 02 · Model your web app in C#
description: Turn a web app idea into classes, properties, interfaces, records, and clear request models.

name: 03 · Collections and LINQ for web data
description: Filter, transform, and look up data while understanding when a LINQ query actually runs.

name: 04 · Async C# without the confusion
description: Understand await, tasks, cancellation, and resource lifetimes without blocking your web server.

name: 05 · Build ASP.NET Core endpoints
description: Follow URLs, query strings, and JSON into a handler, then choose the right HTTP response.

name: 06 · Services, middleware, and configuration
description: Connect services, follow the request pipeline, and give your app the settings and logs it needs.

name: 07 · Persist data with EF Core
description: Follow an entity from C# to the database: queries, tracking, saves, migrations, and conflicting edits.

name: 08 · Validation and web security
description: Validate requests, recognize the caller, and protect each operation and private resource.

name: 09 · Choose and build a .NET web UI
description: Choose between MVC, Razor Pages, and Blazor, then reason about forms, rendering, and state.

name: 10 · Test and debug .NET web apps
description: Write tests that check real behavior and trace a broken request from the browser to storage.

name: 11 · Run a reliable .NET service
description: Bound expensive work, handle failures, and understand what your app needs to run after deployment.

name: 12 · Build a real notes app, one decision at a time
description: Apply what you learned to creating, reading, editing, and shipping a useful notes application.

name: 21 · HTTP and REST in practice
description: HTTP as a CRUD API really uses it: retries, status codes, Content-Type, caching and ETags, CORS preflight, redirects, query strings and curl.

name: 22 · Build a Node and Express API
description: Write a small JSON API with Express 5: routes and params, JSON bodies, middleware order, async errors, 404s, routers, and config.

name: 23 · Logins, sessions, and cookies
description: How a web app remembers who is logged in: session IDs, cookie attributes, login and logout, JWTs, OAuth sign-in, and limits on password guessing.

name: 24 · SQL for everyday CRUD
description: Write the inserts, updates, upserts, join tables, searches, and date filters a CRUD API needs, in PostgreSQL 17 syntax.

name: 25 · React forms and server data
description: Submit forms with FormData and React 19 actions, load and update server data safely, and read route params.

name: 26 · Test a web app with Vitest
description: Write Vitest tests for real web code: matchers, async errors, mocks, fetch stubs, fake timers, Testing Library queries, and API tests.

name: 27 · Debug with browser DevTools
description: Use Chrome DevTools to see the real request, cookie, style or error: Network, Sources, Application and Elements panels, plus device mode and remote debugging.

name: 28 · Review, merge, and deploy
description: Get a pull request reviewed and merged cleanly, then ship it: lockfiles, build-time env vars, SPA hosting, migration order, and smoke checks.

name: 29 · Data modeling and migrations
description: Design tables that stay correct: primary and foreign keys, join tables, constraints, the indexes a new table needs, NULL and defaults, and migration files.

name: 30 · Performance and caching basics
description: Make a working CRUD app fast: time each step, fix N+1 queries and skipped indexes, page without counting, pick a cache layer, and trim React and bundle costs.
